messages:
tara: Quick ping — PR https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4723 updates quantized KV cache eviction logic. Rough summary: ~18% average RAM reduction per inference host in our staging beam, but one trace showed a small throughput regression for short-chat workloads. Can someone with perf/routing context take a quick look? Need merge decision before tomorrow's canary window.

ajay: on it. Can you paste the microbench numbers and the failing trace? Also, which routing tier did you test (latency vs cost)?

tara: Tested on 'latency-preferred' and 'balanced' routing. Microbench (staging, 8k sequences, avg over 6 runs):
```
baseline:  1250 req/s, 64.8 GB mem per host
pr-4723:   1210 req/s, 53.2 GB mem per host
delta:     -3.2% throughput, -17.9% mem
```
Failing trace: short-chat workload (median tokens 24) saw p95 latency +12ms in one run; longer sequences unchanged.

maria: Thanks. The RAM drop is attractive for Dedicated capacity. The p95 blip worries me only if it correlates with batching behavior. Any logs around batch sizes during that run?

tara: Attached the small log excerpt inline:
```
[2026-03-16T18:41:02Z] batch_size=1, active_batches=3, kv_hits=0.82
[2026-03-16T18:41:03Z] batch_size=4, active_batches=2, kv_hits=0.85
[2026-03-16T18:41:04Z] batch_size=1, active_batches=4, kv_hits=0.60  # this coincides with the p95 spike
```

andre: Looks like eviction caused more KV misses for very short inferences; that can force extra attention work per token. Two quick asks: 1) can the eviction be smoothed (delay re-evict for recently cold keys) and 2) add a short-circuit path for batch_size==1 to avoid extra checks. If that's cheap we can keep memory wins and avoid the spike.

sam: CI/status? I can hold the merge if we need fixes before canary.

ci-bot: PR 4723 — All checks passed (unit, lint, integration). Mergeable: true. Merge hold: none.

ajay: My quick local run confirms the pattern: avg throughput -3%, p95 for short-chat +10-14ms on one synthetic. I'll open a tiny patch on top of 4723 to gate the eviction aggressiveness with a knob 'evict_slope=0.5' that can be tuned. If we land that, I expect the p95 to return to baseline.

tara: Thanks — that sounds ideal. If @ajay posts the patch as a stacked PR, can someone from infra + perf give an approval so I can merge before the 09:00 UTC canary? Tagging @maria for infra and @andre for perf. :pray:

maria: I can review and +1 if the knob is config-only and defaults to current behavior (no change unless tuned).

andre: Will review asap, but sounds reasonable. If ajay's change is small and covered by the existing integration tests I'm fine with fast-track.

ajay: Posted: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4724 (small eviction-slope knob + unit tests). Please review.

tara: Great — if we get two approvals in the next 45m, I'll queue both PRs for the 09:00 canary. If not, we'll postpone to the next window and keep 4723 in a staging hold.

sam: Marking blocked->ready depending on approvals. I'll monitor. :eyes:
